title: The Lighter Brief
overview: A gentle mix today: a sunny-but-chilly Sunday in Charlotte, an NFL game in Munich with a rock band at halftime, and a promising Alzheimer's study about spotting early warning signs years ahead. There's also some celebrity back-and-forth, a new leadership book from Jamaica, and a look at how Congress plans to dig into drug-pricing deals.

stories.headline: Montego Bay remembers Deputy Mayor 'Debo' Crawford
stories.summary: Montego Bay Deputy Mayor Dwight 'Debo' Crawford died suddenly at 48, and colleagues across party lines are remembering him for his service. Just two weeks earlier he told young people at a Junior Mayor event that 'leadership is not a title, it is a lifestyle.' He had also worked on recovery in communities hit by Hurricane Melissa.
key_facts: First elected councillor for Spring Garden Division in 2016
Became deputy mayor in March 2024
Spoke to young leaders on October 30
stories.why: His encouragement to young people, 'just be purposeful, be passionate and be you,' is a nice thing to carry forward.

links.title: ‘Leadership is not a title’ - MoBay mourns ‘Debo’ Crawford Deputy mayor, 48, remembered for service beyond political lines

stories.headline: Luz Longsworth: 'Don't let our firsts be our lasts'
stories.summary: Veteran academic and corporate leader Dr Luz Longsworth launched her new book in Montego Bay, arguing that women breaking glass ceilings doesn't mean all barriers are gone. Written as letters to her daughter Marissa, the book urges leaders to look 'below the surface' at hidden office politics, and it includes candid stories from her own career.
key_facts: Book title: Through the Glass Bottom … Navigating Leadership's Hidden Currents
Launch held at Westport in Montego Freeport, St James
She noted Jamaica has had only one female prime minister
stories.why: It's a thoughtful, personal take on leadership that's useful to anyone working their way up.

links.title: We’ve broken the glass ceiling, but have we overcome? – Luz Longsworth

stories.headline: Charlotte: sunny and cool today
stories.summary: Expect a bright but chilly day around Charlotte. Temperatures will drop into the low 30s again overnight.
key_facts: Overnight lows in the low 30s
stories.why: Good day for a walk, but grab a jacket for the evening.

links.title: Sunny but cool for the Charlotte area today

stories.headline: Khloé Kardashian is done with Lamar Odom's comments
stories.summary: On the November 12 episode of The Kardashians, Khloé Kardashian said she's cut ties with ex-husband Lamar Odom after their dispute over his Netflix documentary. She says she took part unpaid to help him, then felt his remarks painted their marriage as a fame move. Odom has denied saying he married her for fame.
key_facts: Documentary 'Untold: The Death & Life of Lamar Odom' came out March 31
They married in 2009; divorce was final in 2016
Her quote: 'The bridge is burned… So he is dead to me'
disputed: Confirmed: Kardashian made these remarks on her show
Disputed: whether Odom said he married her for fame. He said in June, 'That never came out of my mouth'
stories.why: It's the latest chapter in a long, public on-and-off relationship fans have followed for years.

links.title: Khloe Kardashian Slams Lamar Odom Over Marriage Comments: “He’s Dead To Me”

stories.headline: Patriots vs. Lions in Munich, with Cage The Elephant at halftime
stories.summary: The NFL heads to Germany today as the New England Patriots take on the Detroit Lions at FC Bayern Munich Stadium. Grammy-winning rock band Cage The Elephant plays the halftime show, and both national anthems get live performances.
key_facts: Kickoff Sunday, Nov. 15 at 9:30 a.m. ET on FOX
Patriots are 5-4; Lions are 6-2
Sixth NFL regular-season game ever played in Germany
Drew Baldridge sings the U.S. anthem; LaBrassBanda performs Germany's
stories.why: A fun Sunday-morning game with a concert in the middle.

stories.headline: Band stranded in Charlotte while their gear flies ahead
stories.summary: After Friday night's nationwide ground stoppage, most flights are back on track, but some travelers are still catching up. One San Diego alternative band is stuck in Charlotte while its instruments sit in Albany, as the musicians race to make the first stop of their tour.
key_facts: Ground stoppage happened Friday night
The band is starting a nine-city tour
Most flights are back on schedule as of Saturday
stories.why: If you're flying this weekend, it's worth double-checking your flight, though things are mostly back to normal.

links.title: 'Our instruments are in Albany without us.': San Diego-based alternative band stuck in Charlotte after nationwide ground stoppage

stories.headline: Brain-heart signals might hint at recovery after oxygen loss
stories.summary: Researchers at the Paris Brain Institute studied whether the way the brain and heart interact can predict survival after resuscitation from severe oxygen loss. The work builds on earlier findings and is published in the journal eNeuro.
key_facts: Led by Diego Candia-Rivera and Sofia Carrion-Falgarona
Published in eNeuro
disputed: This was done in rats, so it's early-stage research and not yet tested as a tool for people
stories.why: It could one day help doctors better predict recovery for patients.

links.title: Brain–heart interactions may predict recovery from oxygen loss

stories.headline: Alzheimer's may leave early clues up to a decade ahead
stories.summary: Johns Hopkins scientists studying hundreds of brain scans found that two regions, the entorhinal cortex and amygdala, start shrinking before the hippocampus, which is where doctors usually look. These changes are linked to tau protein buildup and could help spot risk years before memory problems begin.
key_facts: Changes may appear as much as 10 years before symptoms
Published in NeuroImage Reports
Being presented at Neuroscience 2026
disputed: This is research based on brain scans. It isn't an approved diagnostic test yet, and the researchers say it 'could eventually' help with earlier detection
stories.why: Earlier detection could give future treatments a better chance to protect the brain.

links.title: Alzheimer’s may start shrinking two brain regions years before memory loss
